getting-started: Install Solenta on macOS, Windows or Linux, add your repository, and choose the agent CLIs you want to run using your own subscriptions or keys.
memory: One local memory server every agent in Solenta reads and writes over MCP, so the next agent starts where the last one stopped. Free and open source.
views: Use Solenta's inbox, issue-backed planboard and review view to follow threads, start tasks from GitHub or GitLab issues, and review agent work.
threads: Choose an agent provider, permission mode and model for each Solenta thread. Follow-up turns resume the same provider session and conversation.
cli-sessions: Import existing agent CLI sessions into Solenta, append new turns on re-import, or eject a thread to continue the provider session in a terminal.
codex: Use interactive Codex sessions in Solenta for live steering, command approvals and model changes, with the limits of each execution path explained.
palette: Find commands, recent threads and projects with Solenta's command palette. Use separate keyboard entry points for commands, file search and thread search.
worktrees: Give each Solenta thread its own Git worktree and branch, inspect its diff, choose files to commit, and review pull requests before merging changes.
workflows: Run multi-phase Build workflows in Solenta. Choose providers per phase, fan work out to several agents, and inspect or retry their results in the app.
orchestration: Delegate work to Solenta worker threads with separate worktrees. Use crew tasks, permissions and handoffs, then review and integrate their results.
guardrails: Protect worker configuration, apply tool guardrails and set a verify command in Solenta. A thread settles green only after verification exits with code 0.
spec: Plan work in Solenta spec mode with separate requirements, design and task artifacts. Review each stage before approving and dispatching its tasks.
teach: Use Solenta Teach mode for hints, reviews and paired work. Autonomy increases through review gates, keeping the session focused on learning.
ask: Ask read-only questions about a repository using Solenta's code index and shared memory, then switch the thread to work when you want implementation.
review: Review Solenta changes in an ordered itinerary built from the diff, with configuration, critical behavior, tests and risks grouped for the reviewer.
skills: Find installed skills in Solenta, manage user skills and MCP servers, and preview imports from Claude Code, Codex or Cursor before copying them.
automations: Schedule Solenta prompts hourly, daily or weekly, run them immediately, and inspect results as threads. Configure project, provider and model per automation.
dev-servers: Start and stop project dev servers from Solenta, follow their logs, and open detected URLs. Learn how thread data directories and claimed ports are isolated.
project-config: Share Solenta setup commands, quick actions, automation definitions and project settings in repository files, with documented precedence for app overrides.
panes: Use Solenta's Chat, Terminal and Browser panes beside the transcript. Learn the terminal session lifecycle and the supported local preview workflow.
spend: Set a daily budget in Solenta to block new runs at the cap, inspect per-thread token usage and cost, and bound the budget for one orchestration.
analytics: Inspect Solenta spending and token usage by provider and model, check provider quota windows, and set prices when a model reports tokens without costs.
integrations: Pair an external MCP client with Solenta's loopback task server. Choose project scope, capabilities and expiry, then revoke the pairing when needed.
updates: Manage Solenta completion notifications, the morning digest and app updates. Learn the release channels and how downloaded updates are verified.
web-mode: Serve Solenta Web from the computer holding your projects and agents, then connect from a phone or browser using the documented connection setup.
ssh: Use Solenta on another computer or connect a project over SSH. Learn which machine owns the agents, threads and worktrees in each connection mode.
windows: Run Solenta on Windows with project checks for Git Bash, Node and WSL boundaries, attached agent processes, and a visible sandbox status for each run.
performance: Understand Solenta's transcript search, bounded history cache and deferred diagnostics. Cache limits describe retained data, rather than total application RAM.
architecture: Understand Solenta's Electron main process, React renderer, typed IPC, CLI provider adapters and local memory supervisor, with links to architecture details.
